title: inset_element adding margins?
description:
Reprex:

```r
library(ggplot2)   # 3.3.3
library(patchwork) # 1.1.1
gg1 <- ggplot(expand.grid(x=0:1, y=0:1), aes(x, y)) +
  geom_path(size = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(expand = 0) +
  theme(
   ,axis.title = element_blank()
   ,axis.text = element_blank()
   ,axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )    
gg2 <- gg1 +
  theme(
   ,panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # bg of the panel
   ,plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA) # bg of the plot
   ,panel.grid.major = element_blank() # get rid of major grid
   ,panel.grid.minor = element_blank() # get rid of minor grid
   ,legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # get rid of legend bg
   ,legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # get rid of legend panel bg
  )
```

`gg1` is straight-forward:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5815808/106183978-f040af80-616e-11eb-8ff6-f6cb6b4069a2.png)

When we `inset_element(gg2,...)` in the upper-right corner, though,

```r
gg1 +
  inset_element(gg2, left = 0.8, right = 1, bottom = 0.8, top = 1)
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5815808/106184168-2e3dd380-616f-11eb-88f5-b6b71cbf936a.png)

Two problems with this:

- the full-plot margins have shifted inwards, and
- the inset plot does not appear to extend from `=0.8` to `=1` in either axis; I would expect a bit of an up/right shift as in

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5815808/106184274-4f062900-616f-11eb-952a-8d91c0708193.png)

(plus not moving the outer margins of the full-plot).

Slightly related, if I remove the `panel.background` and `plot.background` theme elements, we'll see a bit more:

```r
gg3 <- gg1 +
  theme(
   #  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # bg of the panel
   # ,plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA) # bg of the plot
   ,panel.grid.major = element_blank() # get rid of major grid
   ,panel.grid.minor = element_blank() # get rid of minor grid
   ,legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # get rid of legend bg
   ,legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent") # get rid of legend panel bg
  )
gg1 +
  inset_element(gg3, left = 0.8, right = 1, bottom = 0.8, top = 1)
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5815808/106184341-6513e980-616f-11eb-8914-a10912dd8418.png)

showing an added white boundary. In addition to the expected up/right shift from above, I did not expect the white boundary.

Is there a way to maintain the full-plot margins, and to make sure that `top=1` means the top border of the plot region, not just near it?

title: theme_void seems to overwrite guides = "collect"
description:
When using theme_void, guides = "collect" seems to stop working. Maybe theme_void is overwriting themes set by guides = "collect"? Also, global setting such as `& theme(legend.justification = "...")` seems to fail in this case. 


I stumbled upon this on [answering a question on stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66307022/how-to-plot-outside-of-plotting-area-using-ggplot-in-r/66307631#66307631). Interestingly, guides between theme_void plots are being collected. (see last plot in this issue, and the SO example plot)
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(mpg, disp, colour = mpg)) +
  scale_color_continuous(limits = c(0,30)) 

p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(hp, wt, colour = mpg)) +
  scale_color_continuous(limits = c(0,30)) 


p1 + p2 + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/NoZASqj.png)

``` r

p1 + p2 + theme_void() + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/l8qfNqq.png)


It works with other themes
``` r

p1 + p2 + theme_classic() + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/GrkvpnH.png)

When both plots are `theme_void`, it works. 

``` r
p1 + theme_void() + p2 + theme_void()+
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/Zco3J5o.png)

description:
Hi,

I am facing an issue regarding the way `patchwork` deals with plot titles when the text angle is higher than 0. For some reason, instead of aligning the text to the corresponding panel as defined in the `ggplot2` code, `patchwork` aligns titles to each other so that they are centered to the longest text. Having plot titles of the same size does not result in this issue. And this is a new issue I am facing, since using an older version of `patchwork` did not lead to this outcome. I also think this issue is linked to issue #272.

The code I used is the following:

```R
require(ggplot2)
require(patchwork)
require(reshape2)

set.seed(seed = 123)
data(iris)
iris$Sepal.Length.x.Sepal.Width <- iris$Sepal.Length * iris$Sepal.Width
iris <- iris[,sample(x = colnames(x = iris))]

iris.melted <- reshape2::melt(data = iris,
                              id.vars = "Species")

iris.melted.l <- split(x = iris.melted,
                       f = iris.melted$variable)

reference.plot <- names(x = iris.melted.l)[1]

plots.list <- lapply(X = iris.melted.l,
                     FUN = function(variable.data,
                                    reference.plot) {
                       plot.title <- unique(x = variable.data$variable)
                       
                       out.plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(data = variable.data,
                                                   mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = value,
                                                                          y = Species,
                                                                          fill = Species)) +
                         ggplot2::geom_violin(scale = "width",
                                              show.legend = FALSE) +
                         ggplot2::labs(title = plot.title) +
                         ggplot2::theme(axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                        axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                        plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45,
                                                                           hjust = 0,
                                                                           vjust = 0,
                                                                           size = 10))
                       
                       if (plot.title != reference.plot) {
                         out.plot <- out.plot +
                           ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                          axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
                       }
                       
                       return(out.plot)
                     },
                     reference.plot = reference.plot)

combined.plots <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plots.list,
                                        nrow = 1)
```

title: Extend `/` to allow for NULL on terms
description:
Hi Thomas,

In some algorithms, you need to set a plot to `NULL`.

For instance, if you are making plots in a loop, the current plot may have no sense for current parameters, in some limit-cases.

When adding `ggplot` layers with `+`, you can add `NULL` with no error, returning the original object. Would this be possible with `patchwork` also?

In my current task, I'm using patchwork to make a 2x2 plot table. For that, I have to make two 1x2 horizontal patches and then stack them using `/`. Either patch can be `NULL`.

I've been confronted with 2 cases: 

- the lower patch is `NULL`, yielding the error "Only knows how to fold ggplot objects together"
- the upper patch is `NULL`, yielding the error "non-numeric argument to binary operator"

I'm not sure it is even doable (especially for the upper patch), but I'd think extending `patchwork` operators to allow for NULL would make sense, and it would also allow more flexibility in making algorithms.

Here is a reproducible example (simpler than my task):

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
patch <- p1+p1
p2 <- NULL

p1/p2 #works, returns only p1
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/E5rwPje.png)

``` r
patch/p2
#> Error: Only knows how to fold ggplot objects together
p2/p1
#> Error in e1 + e2 + plot_layout(ncol = 1): non-numeric argument to binary operator
```

title: ggsave() to single PDF file

```
print(p)
ggsave(filename = "plots.pdf", plot = marrangeGrob(p, nrow = 1, ncol = 1)) 
```

But when I use patchwork, this doesn't work anymore, as only parts of the patchwork are saved, although print() works fine:

```
library(patchwork)
```

Am I missing something or is there an issue? I don't necessarily need to use marrangeGrob(), but I'd like to save all plots into one PDF file; any other way?

title: Make patchwork arithmetic operators extendable
description:
Hej hej @thomasp85 !

Thank you for the wonderful pkg. I use it often and it's super helpful 🥇 

The first line of code in the arithmetic operator functions is `if (should_autowrap(e2)) e2 <- wrap_elements(full = e2)`. The `should_autowrap()` function is simple, and makes it possible to apply the `wrap_elements()` function to gobs that require it.

```r
should_autowrap <- function(x) {
  is.grob(x) || inherits(x, 'formula') || is.raster(x) || inherits(x, 'nativeRaster')
}
```

I maintain a ggplot-based package for creating survival curves (https://github.com/ddsjoberg/ggsurvfit), and I would love to be able to utilize the patchwork arithmetic operators. To make this work, I would need to perform some pre-processing for my class of plot. To make the patchwork arithmetic operators extendable, we could update this line `if (should_autowrap(e2)) e2 <- wrap_elements(full = e2)` to be a generic instead.

Here's what I had in mind:

```r
#' @export
#' @rdname arithmetic_prep
arithmetic_prep <- function(x, ...) {
  UseMethod("arithmetic_prep")
}

#' @importFrom grid is.grob
#' @importFrom grDevices is.raster
#' @export
#' @rdname arithmetic_prep
arithmetic_prep.default <- function(x, ...) {
  # wrap input plot as needed
  if (is.grob(x) || inherits(x, 'formula') || is.raster(x) || inherits(x, 'nativeRaster')) {
    x <- wrap_elements(full = x)
  }
  x
}
```

By making this a generic function, other package authors could write their own methods to properly handle plots of other classes. If you're amenable to this, I can prepare a pull request. Thanks! 🐟

title: Consider support for tagging faceted plots
description:
Hi @thomasp85,

I'm not sure if this is outside of the scope of `patchwork` but I was wondering if you would ever consider a feature for automatically tagging faceted plots (something like `plot_annotation(tag_levels = ...)`)?

My current workaround to achieve this look is to create single-faceted plots and then using `patchwork` to combine and annotate them. But I would love to simplify this by having an API something like:
```r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

p <- mtcars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(mpg)) +
  geom_density() +
  facet_wrap(~ vs)

p + facet_annotation(tag_levels = ...)
```

This sort of API might allow some nice nesting of plot tags when one of the panels is itself a facet plot that should have its own separate tags. This sort of nested tagging is already supported in `patchwork`, but not for faceted plots.
```r
p1 <- mtcars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(mpg)) +
  geom_density()

p2 <- mtcars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(mpg)) +
  geom_density() +
  facet_wrap(~ vs)

p1 / (p2 + facet_annotation(tag_levels = "1")) & plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

What do you think?

title: Possible regression: invalid 'layout.pos.row'
description:
I am using patchwork to arrange `bayesplot` plots. I'm attaching one such plot, [plot1.zip](https://github.com/thomasp85/patchwork/files/3908812/plot1.zip), which is a `facet_wrap`'ed plot using `ncol = 1`. Use `load("plot1.RData")` to load it.

In the "old" `patchwork` GitHub version (unsure how old, unfortunately, but between two months and a year), this would make two columns as expected:

```r
    plot1 + plot1 
```

However, with the CRAN version 1.0.0, it yields the following error:

```r
Error in grid.Call.graphics(C_setviewport, vp, TRUE) : 
  invalid 'layout.pos.row'
```

I'm just including one plot here, but the issue exists with different `bayesplot` plots as well. `patchwork` 1.0.0 works just fine with "home-made" faceted plots, so it's possible that this is `bayesplot` not conforming to standards. The `grid` package seems to be the origin of the `layout.pos.row` variable.

I don't know if it's of any use, but the following does not raise an error for `nrow >= 2`. Unfortunately, the resulting plot is "stacked" and the y-axis is inverted:

```r
plot1 + plot1 + plot_layout(ncol = 2, nrow = 7)
```

title: Fixed scale coordinate systems forces aspect ratio for plot but not for axes.
description:
Adding a fixed scale coordinate system (such as `coord_equal`, `coord_fixed`, `coord_sf`, `coord_quickmap`, etc) will correctly result in a plot with fixed aspect ratio between `x` and `y`, but the axes will preserve the device aspect ratio. 

```r
library(package = "ggplot2")
library(package = "patchwork")

ggplot(mtcars) +
    geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
    coord_equal() +
        # Add plot to get an assemble (assembly?)
        ggplot(mtcars) +
        geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(nrow = 1)
```

title: Bottom plot title disappears after combining
description:
Seems there might be a bug where patchwork removes the title of a second plot when combined.

Make the basic plots
```
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

ptop <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_point(aes(mpg, disp)) + 
  ggtitle(label = "(a) Panel a",
          subtitle = 'Plot 1') +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_point(aes(mpg, disp)) + 
  ggtitle(label = "",
          subtitle = 'Plot 1') +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear)) + 
  ggtitle(label = "",
          subtitle = 'Plot 2')
  

p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_point(aes(hp, wt, colour = mpg)) + 
  ggtitle(label = "",
          subtitle = 'Plot 3')

p5 <- ggplot(mtcars) + 
  geom_bar(aes(gear)) + 
  facet_wrap(~cyl) + 
  ggtitle(label = "",
          subtitle = 'Plot 4')
```

Top plot looks correct
![ptop](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24922527/139086311-28aa82f6-4b22-4524-a0ae-026fcb057837.png)

Assemble the bottom plot with a title. it looks correct
```
pbot <- p2 + p3 + p4 + p5 + plot_layout(guides = "collect")+ 
  plot_annotation(title = '(b) Panle b') & 
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom',plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) 
```

![pbot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24922527/139086346-65b46c8a-9272-4f59-b225-047f7cc5cdbb.png)

Make the final plot. `pbot` title disappears. 
```
ptop + pbot + plot_layout(ncol = 1)
```

title: Support for ggmatrix
description:
Hi,

Currently, GGally provides the useful function ggpairs, which has no equivalent directly in ggplot. Its output is a ggmatrix, similar to the output of GGally's functin ggmatrix.

Would it be possible to have some kind of support this kind of object?

Otherwise, any suggestions to integrate something that behaves similarly to base R's pairs function?

title: Legend becomes very large in combined plot?
description:
I've been using patchwork and overall it is a great package. I have two issues I dont understand when combining plots with legends. I have three ggplot objects, two of which have unique legends. First, when I try to combine then into rows, the legend from the bottom-right plot seems to be treated like it gets its own column in the layout (see how it sticks out beyond the top plot). Second, and this might be related, the legends always seem to become huge relative to the plot when combined. Are there ways to configure this?

At least as far as the top plot not extending full-width, based on your examples here (https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/articles/guides/layout.html#controlling-guides-1), it seems like maybe this is simply how patchwork handles this?

```
Fig6 <- P1 + P7v + P6 + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') + plot_layout(design = 'AA\nBC')
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7724863/122394204-8f055700-cf2a-11eb-9d6f-6aad951ab3d2.png)

Thanks for any help

title: Automating the patchwork building
description:
Hi,

I have written a function VPM(x) that takes a gene symbol and generates a violin plot using the Seurat::VlnPlot() with some modifications, and then assigns the ggplot2 plot back to the global environment. with the the name "VPM_x".  The reason I'm calling the VlnPlot() within my own function is that I am applying some customizations to the graphs I couldn't figure out just using the VlnPlot() alone. 

I can then use a for (i in x) loop to iterate over a list of Gene Symbols and output multiple "VPM_x" ggplot2 objects, fairly simply.

I'm wondering how to go about programmatically patchworking all of these objects into a single layout, and do it in such a way that it handles different numbers of gene symbols automatically?  I suspect this is possible, as the "Seurat" package, for example, has multiple functions (like VlnPlot()) that automatically generate patchworked objects if the #genesymbols input > 1.  But, I'm too new to coding and do not know how to look at their source to see how it is done.

I have multiple "sets" of gene symbols which represent different types of genes, which are not uniform in length.  So, I would like all of the graphs for each gene symbol "set" to be stacked in one column, allowing the number of rows to adjust to the number of symbols automatically, rather than hard coding each patchwork object.  

Hoping I'm explaining this in a way that makes sense.  I really appreciate the power of the patchwork package!

Robert

title: Any way to customize facet position?
description:
I am plotting a `ggplot2` graph that has an uneven number of facets. My plot currently looks like this:

```
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(group=c(1,1,2,2,3),
                 name=c('a','b','c','d','e'),
                 x=c(1,2,3,4,5),
                 y=c(2,3,4,5,6))
ggplot(df, aes(x,y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ name, ncol=3) 
```

[![enter image description here][1]][1]

Note that the default positioning for the facets is:

```
a b c
d e
```

However, I would like to have a finer control on the positioning of the facets. Specifically, I would like to "center" the bottom two facets in order to distribute the void space more evenly on the sides of the plot.

In other words, the ideal placement for me would look like:

```
a b c
 d e
```

Is this something I can achieve with `patchwork`? How?

  [1]: https://i.stack.imgur.com/Qkq50.png

title: Using `patchwork` in a package
description:
First of all, this is a great package and thank you for developing it.

I want to use `patchwork` in a custom package to automate the production of a compound plot. As part of building the plot I need to use `patchwork`'s methods for the `+`, `/` etc operators. However, I think these methods only become available once `patchwork` is libraried. 

As such, if I call `my_package::my_plot()` without `library(patchwork)`, it fails (even if `patchwork` is a `Imports` depdency in `my_package`). It gives the error ` Can't add chart_2 to a ggplot object`.

Is there an `@importFrom` command I can call to pull in `patchwork`'s `+`, `\` etc operator functions and methods?

Thanks

title: Image grobs aren't treated like normal patches in some cases
description:
Hi Thomas,

Not sure if this is a bug or just a feature not yet implemented (or I'm just doing something wrong), but it seems like images cannot be treated just like ggplot objects for composing patchworks. For the two examples that fail below, they work if logo is replaced with `p1`, a ggplot object.
``` r
library(magrittr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

p1 <- 
  mtcars %>% 
  ggplot(aes(mpg, hp)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme_light()

logo <- system.file('help', 'figures', 'logo.png', package = 'patchwork')
logo <- png::readPNG(logo, native = TRUE)

(p1 / p1) / logo
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/qVw4Bfy.png)

``` r
(p1 / p1) | logo
#> Error: Only knows how to fold ggplot objects together

(p1 | p1) / logo
#> Error: Only knows how to fold ggplot objects together
```

title: Combining plots with plot_layout
description:
Hi!

First of all, thanks for this amazing package. It is simply fantastic!

I have two scattersplots that I want to arrange on the same page. This can normally be achieved trivially by adding them together.


```
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

scat1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, disp)) + geom_point()
scat2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(log10(mpg), log10(disp))) + geom_point()

scat1 + scat2
```


I want to augment both scatter plots with histograms on the side. I achieve this using the `plot_layout` function. It works like a charm for individual scatterplots:

# Plot 1
```
hist1_top <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg)) + geom_histogram()
hist1_right <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp)) + geom_histogram() + coord_flip()
p_fin1 <- hist1_top + 
  plot_spacer() + 
  scat1 + 
  hist1_right + 
  plot_layout(
    ncol = 2, 
    nrow = 2, 
    widths = c(4, 1),
    heights = c(1, 4)
  )
p_fin1

# Plot2
hist2_top <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(log10(mpg))) + geom_histogram()
```

title: Peculiar behaviour with grouped custom geom based on geom_path
description:
I apologise in advance for this long thread. I am not even sure if this is a patchwork issue or simply a poorly written geom. However, the behaviour consistently occurs when using patchwork, and I simply don't understand it... Interestingly, when knitting to html-vignette (!), it also happens with the simple plot (not only with the patchworked one). 

I do understand if you decide that this is poorly written code, but I'd be extremely grateful for even a small hint towards the reason for this benaviour...  

The geom is modified [from this thread on Stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/a/55857158/7941188)

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
```

I have been able to boil the data down to the structure in the test. Factors were not the reason. **Geom**
```r
geom_trail <-
  function (mapping = NULL, data = NULL, stat = "identity", position = "identity",
            na.rm = FALSE, show.legend = NA, inherit.aes = TRUE, ...) {
    layer(data = data, mapping = mapping, stat = stat, geom = GeomTrail,
          position = position, show.legend = show.legend, inherit.aes = inherit.aes,
          params = list(na.rm = na.rm, ...))
  }


GeomTrail <- ggplot2::ggproto(
  "GeomTrail", ggplot2::GeomPoint,
  draw_panel = function(data, panel_params, coord, na.rm = FALSE) {
  
    # must be sorted on group
    data <- data[order(data$group), , drop = FALSE]
    munched <- coord_munch(coord, data, panel_params)
    
    # Default geom point behaviour
    if (is.character(data$shape)) {
      data$shape <- translate_shape_string(data$shape)
    }
    coords <- coord$transform(data, panel_params)
    
    if (unique(coords$size == 0)) {
      my_points <- NULL
    } else {
      my_points <- grid::pointsGrob(
        coords$x,
        coords$y,
        pch = coords$shape,
        gp = grid::gpar(
          col = alpha(coords$colour, coords$alpha),
          fill = alpha(coords$fill, coords$alpha),
          fontsize = coords$size * .pt + coords$stroke * .stroke / 2,
          lwd = coords$stroke * .stroke / 2
        )
      )
    }
    
    # Silently drop lines with less than two points, preserving order
    rows <- stats::ave(seq_len(nrow(munched)), munched$group, FUN = length)
    munched <- munched[rows >= 2, ]
    if (nrow(munched) < 2) {
      return(zeroGrob())
    }
    
    # New behaviour
    ## Convert x and y to units
    x <- unit(coords$x, "npc")
    y <- unit(coords$y, "npc")
    
    # Work out grouping variables for grobs
    n <- nrow(munched)
    group_diff <- munched$group[-1] != munched$group[-n]
    start <- c(TRUE, group_diff)
    end <- c(group_diff, TRUE)
    
    ## Make custom grob class
    my_path <- grid::grob(
      x = x, y = y,
      mult = munched$gap * .pt,
      name = "trail",
      gp = grid::gpar(
        col = alpha(munched$colour, munched$alpha)[!end],
        fill = alpha(munched$colour, munched$alpha)[!end],
        lwd = munched$linesize * .pt,
        lty = munched$linetype,
        lineend = "butt",
        linejoin = "round",
        linemitre = 10
      ),
      vp = NULL,
      ### Now this is the important bit:
      cl = "trail"
    )
    
    ## Combine grobs
    ggplot2:::ggname(
      "geom_trail",
      grid::grobTree(my_path, my_points)
    )
  },
  # Adding some defaults for lines and gap
  default_aes = ggplot2::aes(
    shape = 19, colour = "black", size = 1.5, fill = NA, alpha = NA, stroke = 0.5,
    linesize = 0.5, linetype = 1, gap = .9,
  )
)


makeContent.trail <- function(x){
  # Make hook for drawing
  # Convert npcs to absolute units
  x_new <- grid::convertX(x$x, "mm", TRUE)
  y_new <- grid::convertY(x$y, "mm", TRUE)
  
  # Do trigonometry stuff
  hyp <- sqrt(diff(x_new)^2 + diff(y_new)^2)
  sin_plot <- diff(y_new) / hyp
  cos_plot <- diff(x_new) / hyp
  
  diff_x0_seg <- head(x$mult, -1) * cos_plot
  diff_x1_seg <- (hyp - head(x$mult, -1)) * cos_plot
  diff_y0_seg <- head(x$mult, -1) * sin_plot
  diff_y1_seg <- (hyp - head(x$mult, -1)) * sin_plot
  
  x0 = head(x_new, -1) + diff_x0_seg
  x1 = head(x_new, -1) + diff_x1_seg
  y0 = head(y_new, -1) + diff_y0_seg
  y1 = head(y_new, -1) + diff_y1_seg
  keep <- unclass(x0) < unclass(x1)
  
  # Remove old xy coordinates
  x$x <- NULL
  x$y <- NULL
  
  # Supply new xy coordinates
  x$x0 <- unit(x0, "mm")[keep]
  x$x1 <- unit(x1, "mm")[keep]
  x$y0 <- unit(y0, "mm")[keep]
  x$y1 <- unit(y1, "mm")[keep]
  
  # Set to segments class
  class(x)[1] <- 'segments'
  x
}
```

title: Why are my images upside down and flipped?
description:
I'd like to use patchwork to compose a figure containing pdfs that have been made by other scripts, i.e. where I don't have a ggplot to render.  


```
require(ggplot2)
require(patchwork)
require(magick)


p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))

## Version 1: put scatter above boxplot, works fine.
png("version1.png")
p1 / p2
dev.off()
```

This produces the correct image:
![version1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1095067/85150455-75173280-b24a-11ea-8634-3d3619e3b704.png)

```
## Now lets save the two plots as PDF, pretending we don't have the ggplot
## images that rendered them.
pdf(file="scatter.pdf"); p1; dev.off()
pdf(file="boxplot.pdf"); p2; dev.off()

######################################################################
## now try composing the same plot.

p1 = image_ggplot(image_read("scatter.pdf"))
p2 = image_ggplot(image_read("boxplot.pdf"))

## Version 2: arrgh, the box plot is now on top, and images are flipped.
png("version2.png")
p1 / p2
dev.off()
```
![version2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1095067/85150569-9aa43c00-b24a-11ea-99b5-44b8da078e15.png)

This is wrong in a few ways: the boxplot is now on top (it should be at the bottom); the images are flipped, and the top and bottom of the images are truncated.

I can fix the flipping of the imags, but the rest is still wrong:

```
p1 = image_ggplot(image_flip(image_read("scatter.pdf")))
p2 = image_ggplot(image_flip(image_read("boxplot.pdf")))

png("version3.png")
p1 / p2
dev.off()
```

![version3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1095067/85150691-c6272680-b24a-11ea-938a-d510d72e949e.png)


What am I missing?

CC: @nuest

title: strange problem under a fixed aspect coordinates
description:
Thanks for developing such a nice package. 

There's a very strange problem under a  fixed aspect coordinates,  and here's a simple example to reproduce the problem.

```
df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = rnorm(10))
df2 <- expand.grid(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)
df2$value <- rnorm(100)
df3 <- data.frame(x = runif(10, 0, 3), y = 1:10)

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 10.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed()

p2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 10.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 10.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed()

p3 <- ggplot(df3, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 10.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed()
```

title: Black line boxes around plots
description:
First of all, Thomas, thank you for creating such an elegant solution.

So I've been trying to export a plot matrix to png with a transparent background. For a while, I was just getting a white background, but I found a way to get transparency. Now, it's giving me these weird boxes around the plots, and I can not for the life of me figure out why. Have I accidentally triggered some function in patchwork()? Here's an image of what's happening. I have included reproducible example code at the end; it's a little sloppy but it has what I'm really using in there for the most part.

![matrix_example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38814826/82097886-cc693680-96d1-11ea-8a09-f1f24e80486f.png)




if (!require('tidyverse')) install.packages('tidyverse'); library('tidyr')
if (!require('ggplot2')) install.packages('ggplot2'); library('ggplot2')
if (!require('ggthemes')) install.packages('ggthemes'); library('ggthemes')
if (!require('patchwork')) install.packages('patchwork'); library('patchwork')


#######################################################
# Generate data on a hypothetical individual with means
#######################################################
one_person <- 
  data.frame(Category = c("perf_driven"),
             old_average = sample(800:900, 1, replace = TRUE),                         
             self_eval = sample(700:800, 1, replace = TRUE),
             mgr_eval = sample(700:800, 1, replace = TRUE),
             peer_eval = sample(700:800, 1, replace = TRUE)
  )

################################################
# Horizontal bar plots
################################################

horizontal_bars <- function(data_object,metric) { 
  .e<-pivot_longer(data_object, -Category, names_to = "Survey", values_to = "Score")

  .e <- .e %>%
    subset(Category==metric)
    
  ggplot(.e,aes(Category, Score, fill = Survey)) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity", position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE, padding=0), width = .5) +
    coord_flip() +
    geom_text(aes(label=Score), position=position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE, width=.5), hjust=1.1, size = 2.5) +
    #geom_text(aes(label = Score, hjust=0)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent",colour = NA)
    )
  
}

################################################
# Theme for transparency
################################################


transparent_bg_theme =
  theme(
    # panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"), # bg of the panel
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA), # bg of the plot
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"), # get rid of legend bg
    legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent")
    
  )


##################################################
# Create plots and plot matrix (the real version has all different plots)
##################################################

a1 <- horizontal_bars(one_person,"perf_driven")

widths = c(.8,.8)
height = .5
plot_matrix = a1 + a1 + 
  a1 + a1 +
  a1 + a1 +
  a1 + a1 +
  a1 + a1
  
plot_matrix = plot_matrix + plot_layout(ncol = 2, nrow = 5, widths = widths, heights = height)
plot_matrix <- plot_matrix & transparent_bg_theme


##################################################
# Output png file
##################################################

ggsave('matrix_example.png', plot = plot_matrix, height=7, width=2.5, units="in", dpi="print", type="cairo", bg = 'transparent')

title: aligning ranges in layout
description:
Many times I find that creating the plots independently in different geoms the continuous axes are not aligned. Is there an efficient way to align axis ranges of plots in a layout. There is not a great way to retrieve axes limits/ranges from gg objects given that the plot only renders on print or in `ggplot2::ggplot_build` which basically captures the printed object (see code below).

This solution is very inefficient larger gg objects since you would need to build each plot to ascertain the ranges before actually rendering the layout, so you are rendering the layout multiple times to achieve synchronized axes limits/ranges.

Is there any other way to do this, that would not invoke the whole plot to be rendered? 

ref: https://github.com/mjskay/tidybayes/issues/246

```r
axis_rng <- function(p,axis = c('x','y')) {
  
  g <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)
  
  axis <- match.arg(axis,several.ok = TRUE)
  
  names(axis) <- axis
  
  lapply(axis,function(x){
    g$layout[[sprintf('panel_scales_%s',x)]][[1]]$range$range   
  })
  
}
```

title: More complete "current plot" interface?
description:
I think it's a really cool feature to be able to add additional elements to a patchwork and have it be added to one of the plots, this justifies "-" operator to add to the left and make the left plot the "current plot" for adding geoms and such.

However I'm in a situation where I have a marginal plot on the bottom, and would like my top plot to be the "current plot", and as far as I can tell there is no operator for that. I propose that a series of verb functions be added to complete the API that look something like

* `add_top(p1, p2)`
* `add_bottom(p1, p2)`
* `add_left(p1, p2)`
* `add_right(p1, p2)`

possibly with the interface `add_*(p1, p2, focus = TRUE)` to choose whether or not the latest plot is the plot in focus. I don't know how difficult this would be to implement but I imagine you keep a list of ggplots somewhere and it should be possible to keep an index variable tracking which plot is in focus.

title: Patchwork ignores 'outer margin' of plots (set by theme(plot.margin=...))
description:
Patchwork ignores the 'outside' plot margin for the plots. The only theme(plot.margin=...) patchwork seems to respond to, is the 'inner' margin between plots (e.g. right margin for left plot or left margin for the right plot).  I often need to adjust theme(plot.margin=...) when I have axis text labels or geom_text that extend beyond the plot. 

My current solution has been to create empty blank plots using geom_blank() but it ends up being complicated when combining many plots. Can you help resolve the problem in a better way?

``` r

library(reprex)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# ======================= CODE ======================= #

### Plot with extra margins 
# wide top and left margin
p1.outer_margin <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp)) + theme(plot.margin = unit(c(5,1,1,5), "cm")) 
# wide top and right margin
p1.inner_margin  <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp)) + theme(plot.margin = unit(c(5,5,1,1), "cm")) 

### Make another plot
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))

### Patchwork ignores margin arguments
p1.outer_margin + p2 # left and top margins for p1.outer_margin are ignored
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/uhdNkes.png)

``` r
p1.inner_margin + p2 # this correctly displays extra 'inner margin' (right), but the top margin is still ignored
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/LuDPud8.png)

``` r

### Plot_spacer() can be used to add outer margins, but it does not offer the same control as theme(plot.margin=...)
plot_spacer() + p1.inner_margin + p2
```

title: Resolve name conflicts: as_grob()
description:
Both cowplot and patchwork define generics `as_grob()`. However, cowplot exports it and patchwork does not. It seems like the easiest solution for now, to avoid any immediate problems, would be to rename the internal patchwork function. If you agree, I'm happy to prepare a PR.

Going forward, we should have a discussion of what this type of function should do and where it should live. The main difference I see is that your function doesn't open a background device for `as_grob.ggplot()` whereas mine does. I think both approaches are needed. When you're calling `as_grob.ggplot()` during the final output phase, for example as part of a `ggsave()` call, then opening a background device is not needed (and is actually harmful). But if you're calling `as_grob.ggplot()` before final output is generated, e.g. because you're aligning plots that will be output later, then not having an open background device can cause weird bugs in some settings, at least it has done so for me in the past (https://github.com/wilkelab/cowplot/issues/24 https://github.com/wilkelab/cowplot/issues/51 https://github.com/wilkelab/cowplot/issues/73 https://github.com/wilkelab/cowplot/issues/82).

title: Plots using `coord_fixed()` are not using available space
description:
First off, great work and I started using the package almost daily!

I was wondering what are your thoughts on arranging the canvas space plots take if one of two is adjustable and the other is not.

Considering the following example:

```r
cars = tibble::rownames_to_column(mtcars, "name")
p1 = ggplot(cars, aes(x=vs, y=name)) + geom_tile() + coord_fixed()
p2 = ggplot(cars, aes(x=disp, y=name)) + geom_point()
p1 + p2
```

Here, the width of `p1` is defined given its height because of `coord_fixed()`, and the width of `p2` adapts to the canvas size if plotted in isolation. (Resize plot in x and y direction to make this more obvious.)

The way *patchwork* currently handles this is to assume `p1` and `p2` will occupy half of the canvas, unless otherwise specified by `plot_layout()` (which I do not always know in advance).

It would be nice if there was a way to tell `p2` to fill up the available space (or it would do so automatically when `p1` is of fixed size).

title: legend.justification not preserved
description:
My end goal is to produce a pair of plots with a shared legend.  I didn't see this implemented in patchwork yet (although I see a few issues reports which suggest it's on the to-do list - count me in as interested!).  In the meantime, I decided my optimal solution was to produce a horizontal legend across the bottom of one plot, and align it to the right-hand side of the right-most plot.  On an individual graph, this would be changed using `legend.position = bottom` and `legend.justification = right` in `theme()`.  When combining the plots using patchwork, the justification option is ignored and the legend is centered in the graph.  (This is made very obvious if the legend is longer than the graph, and part of it is cut-off).  Here's a reproducible example which illustrates the issue:

``` r
data(iris)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(magrittr)
```

description:
Hi Thomas, once again thanks for this great package! Found out about `plot_annnotation()` and was so happy to see it here - however, it seems to me that the title font gets cut when using plot_annoation() with a custom theme: 

``` r
library(ggplot2)
#> Warning: Paket 'ggplot2' wurde unter R Version 3.5.2 erstellt
library(patchwork)
library(extrafont)
#> Registering fonts with R

theme_custom <- theme_bw() %+replace% 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"))

theme_set(theme_custom)

(ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()) +
  (ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, qsec)) + geom_point()) +
```

title: Feature request: Switch active plot
description:
Loving patchwork! I would really love a way to switch the "active" plot. I can see in [arithmetic.R](https://github.com/thomasp85/patchwork/blob/master/R/arithmetic.R#L10) that the last plot added is the active one, but could we have a function to switch that? 

I feel like generally you'd like users to adjust things ahead of time at the ggplot2 individual plot level, but from a developer's standpoint, imagine that I wanted to make it really easy to create a multi-plot chart using `patchwork`. I'd return to the user a multi-plot like the one below, but then they could only adjust the bottom plot (added last) after the fact. If they could have a "switch active plot" feature then they could adjust any feature of the resulting chart. I think this could be pretty neat for maximum flexibility.

![screen shot 2018-01-23 at 11 28 43 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19150088/35288805-ac931bfa-0033-11e8-8f99-732daa20607f.png)


<details>
<summary>A reprex of what I mean</summary>

The basic idea is:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = as.factor(vs))) +
  geom_bar()
  
my_grouped_plot <- p1 + p2 + plot_layout(ncol = 1)

# Can access the second plot ("active")
my_grouped_plot +
  labs(title = "hello world")
```

title: Add a way to label the plots like A, B, C etc.
Using shiny::nearPoints() with patchwork
description:
Hi, thanks for the great work on this.

Is it possible to use the nearPoints() function from shiny to get the distance from the click to the coordinates of data at a particular subplot built with patchwork? I'm not sure what distance is being returned. Maybe this is a question for the shiny team?

Here is a minimal example, note the dist_ column printed to console.

```
library(shiny)
library(patchwork)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(
  tags$head(tags$style("#plt{height:95vh !important}")),
  plotOutput("plt", click = "plt_click")
))

server <- function(input, output) {

  # dummy data
  x <- y <- 1:10
  df <- expand.grid(x, y)
  names(df) <- c("x", "y")
  df$z <- rnorm(nrow(df))
  
  # define plots
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = z))
  p1 <- p2 <- p3 <- p + geom_tile()
  
  output$plt <- renderPlot({
    (p1|p2)/p3 + plot_layout(ncol = 1, height = c(1, 2))
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$plt_click, {
    
    # clicked coords:
    print(c(input$plt_click$x, input$plt_click$y))
    
    # gives nonsense:
    print(nearPoints(df = df,
                     coordinfo = input$plt_click,
                     xvar = "x",
                     yvar = "y",
                     allRows = T,
                     addDist = T))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: subplot title margins change when coordinates are fixed
description:
Hi Thomas,

When making a multi-panel map plot, I discovered that the margins between the subplots and their titles changed compared to when just viewing the subplots by themselves. 

Reproducible example below:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(rworldmap)
library(patchwork)

# Use country polygons for example
cntrys <- tidy(countriesCoarse)

# Plot A
pA <- ggplot(cntrys, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "#375166") +
  coord_fixed(xlim =c(-85.5,-57.4),ylim = c(9.95,30)) + # bug appears to be related to using fixed coordinates
  labs(title = "Blue map",
       subtitle = "The world is very blue") +
  theme_minimal()

# Print individual plot - title margin looks fine
pA

# Plot B
pB <- ggplot(cntrys, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "#BE2A28") +
  coord_fixed(xlim =c(-85.5,-57.4),ylim = c(9.95,30)) +
  labs(title = "Red map",
       subtitle = "The world is very red") +
  theme_minimal()

# Print multipanel plot
pA + pB + plot_layout(ncol = 1)
```

I believe the issue is related to using `coord_fixed()` - the problem goes away when this is not used and only effects the subplots that use `coord_fixed()`

title: Error handling when assembling plots
description:
I'm using patchwork to generate a multi-page PDF of assembled plots using different underlying data. Think of it as your `README` example

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p1 + p2
```

but instead of this one plot I am plotting it for `n` different cars.

However, not all cars have got the exact same underlying data, and some may be missing a field in their `data.frame` that causes `ggplot` to produce an error when building the subplot. An example for this is when I use `facet_wrap` on a variable that has no observations.

So far, I check each of these errors manually using the code:

```r
if (class(try(ggplot_build(p1))) == "error")
    p1 = element_blank()
if (class(try(ggplot_build(p2))) == "error")
    p2 = element_blank()
# ... same for every element
```

This way, however, I have the build the plot twice: once for checking if it can be built, and once to actually assemble it via `patchwork`.

It would be nice if `patchwork` could handle failed plots automatically, by either leaving them empty or plot the error message instead of the panel.

One option could be to include an error handling function in `plot_layout`:

```r
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(error = function(e) element_blank())
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(error = function(e)
    ggplot(data.frame(error=e), aes(x=1, y=1)) + annotate(label=e))
```

title: API semantics
description:
Being more direct, patchwork's API is certainly a nice improvement over `gridExtra::grid.arrange()`. However, its use of `+` is somewhat awkward, semantically:

- It's used to juxtapose plots, but juxtaposition is not commutative.

- In an expression like `(ggplot(...) + ...) + (ggplot(...) + ...)`, the `+` inside the parentheses and the `+` between the parentheses are altogether different operators. Likewise, the two `+`'s in the expression `p1 + p2 + plot_layout(...)` are completely different (the first describes the topology of the layout, whereas the second describes a rigid geometric mapping onto a plane; `plot_layout()` and the like might be better off applied using `%>%`, say).

`*` might be a semantically more suitable as an operator for juxtaposition, since it is conventionally noncommutative and unused in ggplot2.

On the other hand, an advantage of using `+` is its familiarity from ggplot2. Maybe that's a good enough reason for patchwork ... (But unless I'm mistaken, I believe the author of ggplot2 considers its use of `+` as a less-than-optimal design.)

title: Small plots with coord_quickmap()
description:
This probably applies to other kinds of fixed ratio plots, but it seems like patchwork is leaving too much whitespace, resulting in tiny little plots. 

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

df <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 360, by = 3), 
                        y = seq(-90, 0, by = 3))
df$z <- with(df, x*y)

fplot <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
        geom_tile() +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
        coord_quickmap()

fplot +
    fplot +
    plot_layout(ncol = 1)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/EXJO4El.png)

Cowplot, on the other hand, makes a much better use of space.

``` r
cowplot::plot_grid(fplot, fplot, ncol = 1)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/dfgHNHV.png)

(Identical to `gridExtra::grid.arrange(fplot(1), fplot(2), ncol = 1)`)
